scenes.text: Same AI. Same question. So why do some people get amazing answers, and others get junk? [1] The secret is the prompt. [2] Today, prompt engineering.

title: Prompt
Engineering
data.subtitle: Talk to AI like a pro

scenes.text: A prompt is simply the instruction you give an AI. [1] Prompt engineering means writing that instruction clearly, so the AI knows exactly what you want. [2] Better input. [3] Better output. [4] Fewer retries.

data.definition: Writing clear instructions so the AI knows exactly what you want.

scenes.text: Look at this. [1] Write about my product. The reply is vague and generic. [2] Now let's build a better prompt. First, a role. You are an expert marketer. [3] Then context. My brand sells handmade coconut soaps from Kerala. [4] The task. Write an Instagram caption for our new jasmine soap. [5] And the format. Under forty words, friendly, three hashtags. [6] Now the reply is exactly what we wanted.

data.heading: Build a better prompt

scenes.text: Four power moves. [1] Give examples. Show one or two samples of what you want. That's called few shot prompting. [2] Ask it to think step by step, for maths and logic. [3] Set constraints. Word limits, tone, language. [4] And iterate. Treat it like a conversation, and refine.
Real life uses. [1] Get your resume reviewed, the way a recruiter would. [2] Draft a polite WhatsApp reply to your landlord. [3] Turn messy meeting notes into a clean summary with action items.
Myth! [1] Prompt engineering needs secret magic words. [2] Not really. It's just clear communication. If a smart new intern would understand your instruction, the AI will too.

data.fact: It's clear communication. If a smart new intern would understand it, so will the AI.
